target_customer: Web and mobile developers and small teams who wanted to run sites and apps from spreadsheets and documents
problem: Building a site or app needed custom databases and server infrastructure even for simple content that already lived in spreadsheets.

founders.name: Ted Benson
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page the company grew from his MIT research. He later led machine intelligence and platform teams at Instabase.

founders.name: Jake Lau
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no background.

technical_complexity.rationale: Two-way sync between spreadsheets, documents and web content across Google and Microsoft platforms needed solid integration work, built on MIT research.

defensibility.rationale: Projects built on the platform created some lock-in, but spreadsheet-to-API tools were easy for others to build and platform owners could add the feature.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Instabase acquired the team, announced 2018-02-14. The product stayed live without new features.

market_need_then: Many developers and small organizations already kept content in spreadsheets, and the founder reported tens of thousands of users managing sites from spreadsheets, word documents and design files.

branding.domain_note: cloudstitch.com now redirects to a GoDaddy for-sale page; the product used cloudstitch.io per a StackShare profile.

brand_strength.rationale: Only developer comparison listings mention it. No source shows brand press or community.

outcome_analysis: Cloudstitch came out of MIT research and joined YC in Summer 2015, then was acquired by Instabase with the deal announced on 2018-02-14. The founder said development of new features stopped and support was scaled back, which reads as a team acquisition rather than a product outcome. No funding round was verified, so the strength of the exit cannot be judged.
notes: Website cloudstitch.com is dead (parked for sale). Aggregators (Bounce Watch, Village) show an unverified 800K seed in August 2016 led by Green Visor Capital and 140K in August 2015; CB Insights shows about 120K from YC. None confirmed by a primary source, so no rounds recorded. YC page and Benson's bio say 2017 while the announcement is dated February 2018, likely close in 2017 and announced in 2018 (not stated). Competition search found only later-dated comparison pages, so no dated competitor list is given; Sheetsu, Airtable and others are later or undated comparisons.
